new_title: Warwickshire close on title as Somerset hopes fade: county cricket final round, day two - as it happened
old_text:
Olly Stone also has Adam Lyth in his back pocket at Trent Bridge and Yorkshire are now 50-3.
Surrey have finished on 422 at Taunton. Josh Thomas and Tom Lammonby stride out to open the batting for Somerset's reply and they will face... Dan Lawrence's 'judderman' spin in the first over!
We are still off here at Edgbaston although it is brightening up a little. A gaggle of groundstaff loiter in the middle and stare at the sky.
News:
Somerset didn't get the third bowling bonus point at Taunton which means that once if/when Warwikshire get to 250 they will only need a draw here to guarantee the Championship title.
Bad light stops play here at Edgbaston, I told you it was murky. The weather forecast isn't wet but there is a symbol for dark clouds lurking throughout the day. Hmmm. Hopefully it blows over soon enough.
Surrey are 378-8 in Taunton with the non bat owning Dan Worrall at the crease alongside Adam Thomas. Lofty heights.
Worrall does own a guitar though, I saw some clips of him strumming away on the boundary edge yesterday with just a hint of David Brent/gap year campfire energy...
Grey clouds here at Edgbaston and the floodlights are beaming down. Barnard and Hain are untroubled though and have built the lead to an already tricksy 41. A significant first innings lead and my moolah could be drifting towards this finishing today...
Hampshire are staring down a significant barrel at the Utilita, Eddie Jack has just been castled by Jaydev Unadkat to leave them 69-6 and trailing Sussex by a whopping 175 runs.
This is good insight into Leicestershire's predicament from BBC Leicester's Adam Whitty:
Talking to assistant coach James Taylor last night, what I found interesting was that the Foxes' relegation (as it stands) was essentially ignored - it was as if it hadn't happened.
They want to finish in style but are also confident their appeal against their 27-point deduction can be successful. Had they not had that hit, they would be eight points clear of Essex, and, with one bowling point each so far, still would be.
So that will be their aim. A hammering here and the deduction won't matter."
"At Lord's today to see if the mighty Northamptonshire can bat all day. Well, at least past lunch. Seemed a strange decision to bat first yesterday. I grew up during the heyday of the NatWest Trophy cup finals in September, so maybe the Northamptonshire think tank should have involved me..."
Well, Procter and Vasconcelos have made steady progress to 18-0 ... lunch is still a while off though!
Josh Hull is summoned at Edgbaston and he very nearly cleans up Barnard with his first delivery that hoops back and passes the off stump by the width of a gnat's eyebrow. Two types of leave as they say and that must go down as a 'good one' from the Bears captain.
Nerves in the Garden? Kent need a minimum of 15 points to gain promotion and have three batting points in the bag already. Hang on though, Langridge gets rid of Sam Northeast with his first ball!
Muyeye is back in the hutch now too as Langridge gets his third wicket!
Hello and welcome to day two of the final round of the 2026 County Championship. I'm on the way to Edgbaston where there is a chance Warwickshire are crowned today... or this being cricket, something completely different happens. That's why we love it.
Catch up on a round up of yesterday's action below. I'll post the scores on the doors and we'll get into all the talking points.
Please do get in touch and chat away below the line, enjoy yourselves, it's later than you think.
Day One Report:
The champagne is on ice in Warwickshire but probably not for much longer. Fourteen wickets fell on the opening day at Edgbaston and 10 of them belonged to relegation scufflers Leicestershire who won the toss in late September sunshine and decided to bat first.
A couple of hours later and the Foxes were bowled out for just 125. Baby-faced assassin Ethan Bamber continued his fine season with the ball, the 27-year-old took four for 42 to go level with Hampshire's Kyle Abbott as the leading wicket-taker in Division One this year. It was the seventh innings in succession that the Bears have routed their opponents for under 200. They finished the day five runs ahead with six wickets in hand and have at least a few digits on the trophy.
Asa Tribe scored his second century in successive innings as Glamorgan reached 318 for three against Essex in Cardiff. The bowling point Essex picked up is likely enough to see Leicestershire relegated. An asterisk comes in the form of the appeal the chief executive Emma White confirmed the Midlands club had lodged with the independent Cricket Discipline Panel after they were handed a 27-point deduction for a poor pitch in their match against Glamorgan in the ninth round.
Any chance of a Mexican standoff in the race for the title was de-escalated by Surrey racking up 327 for four against second-placed Somerset. Dan Lawrence going to his sixth century of the campaign with a howitzer six into the stands off Jack Leach. The sun setting along with Somerset's hopes of a hoodoo breaking Championship title late in the day at Taunton.
At Trent Bridge, third-placed Nottinghamshire slipped from a well-placed 172 for four to finish on 242for nine against Yorkshire and in the battle of the south coast Hampshire slipped to 55for four in reply to Sussex's 244.
In Division Two, Northamptonshire's hopes of promotion were dashed by the decision to bat first at Lord's, Middlesex's Ryan Higgins taking four for 30 with the ball to skittle the visitors for 103 and then scoring 115 off 124 balls as the home side posted 255 in response.
Kent started the day in the box seat for the second promotion place behind champions Durham and are 77 for one replying to Gloucestershire's 229 at Canterbury.
Emilio Gay scored his fourth ton of the season for Durham as they cruised to 355 for five against a beleaguered Lancashire at Old Trafford. Worcestershire lead Derbyshire by 131 runs, Ben Allison pocketing five for 22 to raze Wayne Madsen's side for 88 in their first innings.
new_text:
Warwickshire close on title, Kent lead promotion race
James Wallace
Warwickshire made serene progress towards a ninth county championship title on a cloudy day at Edgbaston. A delay for autumnal mid-morning bad light in Birmingham curtailed their progress briefly in the first session but captain Ed Barnard and Sam Hain were as unbothered by the lingering nimbus as they were Leicestershire's bowlers.
Barnard fell caught behind for 88 but Hain was the last man out for 142. Ethan Bamber and Chris Woakes struck in fading light to leave Leicestershire 55-3 and still adrift by 192 runs. A third two-day victory in a row was kiboshed by early evening gloom but Saturday will surely see Warwickshire clinch the 2026 trophy.
Somerset's slim title hopes fizzled like flat cider in Taunton, their failure to take a third bowling bonus point as Surrey amassed 422 meant that Warwickshire can draw and still take the spoils.
Last season's winners Nottinghamshire reduced Yorkshire to 179 all out in their first innings. Olly Stone sent Jonny Bairstow's middle stump for the sort of cartwheel Simone Biles would be proud of as he took five wickets at Trent Bridge. However, bad news filtered through in the afternoon that Stone was injured - reportedly a hamstring - and it was serious enough for him to be immediately withdrawn from the match.
Asa Tribe fell short of a double century in Cardiff but his 184 helped Glamorgan amass 505 in their first innings against Essex who then collapsed at the foot of the mountain on 100 for seven. Sussex are well on top of Hampshire at Southampton, Jaydev Unadkat's five for 32 saw the home side skittled for 128 in response to 244.
In Division Two, a defiant century from Ben Compton at Canterbury kept Kent's promotion prospects in the balance as they made 353 and then took two Gloucestershire wickets to leave the visitors 63 runs shy.
Fellow promotion chasers Northamptonshire fought back to 249 for seven against Middlesex but a slender lead of 97 runs will need to thicken on the hob if they are to set a challenging chase.
Durham defied some mizzly Manchester weather and Lancashire's bowlers to post 493 in their first innings. Worcestershire are in control against Derbyshire, where a fourth-innings chase of over 300 already looks out of reach.
That's me done for today. Tanya will be back on her rightful throne tomorrow to call the final destination of the 2026 title. Thanks for your company and comments, it's been great fun. Goodnight!

Popping back to say they did pop back on at Edgbaston and it was time enough for Chris Woakes to pin Steve Eskinazi bang in front to leave Leicestershire 55-3 when the light faded again and this time it was final, the title will be decided tomorrow.
I'm going to start writing up for the second edition now that the action has been curtailed here. Will be back later on for final knockings of day two. Do keep chatting below the line.
That's the end of the wickets flurry here at Edgbaston, the light is very bad and the umpires take them off. That could be it for the day. The trophy remains just out reach for Warwickshire for one more night.
Exclusive: Ali Martin is here with me and he gets the intel that Olly Stone's injury is a hamstring. Hopefully it is not much more than a twinge. He took his 50th wicket of the season today and his fifth five wicket haul.
Gone and gone! In very gloomy light here at Edgbaston Ethan Bamber pins Sheridon Gumbs plum lbw and then does Rishi Patel with a ripper than is angled in and nips away to kiss the off bail. Two wickets in three balls, they can't do it tonight, can they? It might be the bad night that puts the kibosh on another two dayer.
Surrey's Rahul Chahar is ill and has been replaced by Ralphie Albert in Taunton. Somerset are chipping away at 202-3 with the fifty up for Tom Abell. They still trail by 199 runs, mind.
Warwickshire have been a bit loose with the new ball so far as they hunt the wickets to win the title. Sol Budinger has climbed into three pull shots to short pitched balls and sent each one skittering to the fence.
Gumbs and Budinger come out to open for Leicestershire. Ethan Bamber starts with the new Dukes... slings one down the leg side and all the Warwickshire players go up for a caught behind off the first ball! It isn't out, settle down lads. Tricky batting conditions in fading light and the floodlights blaring.
Essex have slipped to 36-3 in response to Glammy's mountainous total in Cardiff. Zain ul Hassan has just splattered Charlie Allison's stumps to bring Matt Critchley to the middle.
Right then, Sam Hain is the last man out for Warwickshire at Edgbaston. He walks off with 142 runs to his name and gets a great hand from the fans and handshakes from the Leicestershire players too. A classy touch from the visitors.
The lead is 247, now it is a case of wickets v fading light!
Oh no. This is so unfortunate for a bowler who has battled back from injury so many times. Stone has pulled up with something and it is serious/concerning enough to see Nottinghamshire substitute him Tom Giles for the remainder of the match.
Has Dean Elgar played his final innings for Essex? The South African is retiring at the end of this campaign and has just fallen at Cardiff to Timm van der Gugten. Uh oh! Essex lose Paul Walter too and are in the mire at 6-2 and trailing by a whopping 498 runs.
Righto, I'm back after filing for first editions. The players have just come back on at a gloomy again Edgbaston. Ethan Bamber plays a beautiful cover drive on the up and there's more than a whiff of certainty in the air. Warwickshire lead by 212 runs.
"Slow going" reports Guy Hornsby from Old Trafford.
"but Noman Ali has plugged away at the Brian Statham end and bagged himself a five-fer with accurate, probing left arm spin. Rawalpindi it most certainly isn't, but he's worked hard today. If Lancashire can prise out the last couple here, they'll get another go at passing 200, something they've only managed once in the last 5 rounds of Division 2 cricket. It's the hope that kills you, etc etc."
Steady accumulation here at Edgbaston as Hain moves into the 90s and the lead is up to 149. I have to write an early report for the paper but will be back later on. Look after the place for me.
Away from the action for a moment. We have to ask - has KP mellowed? It is easy being him nowadays? Ali has the latest from England's new coaching appointment:
The early signs are encouraging, however, with a far more relaxed Pietersen said to now be able to laugh at himself when the piss-taking has flown in this first fortnight. Co-commentators during his occasional television work say the same. And going by his chat with the written media - an industry he recently wrote off and has not entirely trusted in the past - he sounds genuinely energised to shape a side that, beyond Root and Jos Buttler, is learning 50-over cricket on the job.
I'm 46 now. That stuff is so long gone," he said. "I'm a completely different person too. I live in the countryside. I live in South Africa. I love doing what I do. I'm just here to help Brendon, first and foremost, to help the players try and become the best versions of themselves.
I've been lucky to have worn every T-shirt that an England cricketer can wear: the good, the bad, and the unhappy. And so there are parts to all of their careers which I think that I could potentially help them to stay away from the unhappy.
Most of you guys covered a lot of my career. Morning to night I was relentless in my pursuit to be the best version of myself. Since that first call [from McCullum] came in I just talked about the non-negotiables of how I believe each person should live in a dressing room and the full commitment. How I think we can get better as individuals, as a team, and be successful and consistent."
The Pears are bruising a little at New Road. Worcs have slipped to 62-5 and lead Derbyshire by 188, Abbas, Potts and Reece in the wickets for the visitors.
Sunshine peeping through now at Edgbaston as Hain and Barnard make steady progress and extend their lead to 75.
Dan Lawrence bowling and getting some turn at Taunton. A quick foray below the line suggests people are into it, he's such a likeable and unique cricketer. I hope he makes his mark for England.
Olly Stone also has Adam Lyth in his back pocket at Trent Bridge and Yorkshire are now 50-3.

We are still off here at Edgbaston although it is brightening up a little. A gaggle of groundstaff loiter in the middle and stare at the sky.
